To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The instability of time-periodic flow in the presence of curved streamlines is a type of Taylor-Gortler vortex instability, and is spatially localised near the most unstable position.
the instability of some time-periodic flows is similar to the instability of a steady flow and is localized near the most dangerous positions.

1) the instabilities of some time-periodic flows have a similar character to that of Taylor-Görtler vortices in curved boundary layers, 2) these instabilities can be described by a single equation which is a special case of the Orr-Sommerfeld equation, and 3) when nonlinear effects are considered the instability modifies the time-averaged flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the stability of spatially and/or temporally varying flows, in particular the instability of flows with curved stream lines and the instability of flows which can induce steady streaming boundary layers.
the instability of time-periodic motions and the resulting modifications of the time-averaged flow.
the study of time-periodic fluid flows and their stability, and the effects of nonlinearities on their stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a time-periodic flow can be stable, unstable, or neutral, depending on the flow and the frequency of oscillation.
the instabilities of time-periodic motions are not necessarily more complicated than those of steady motions.
the instability is a consequence of the presence of a finite amplitude of the fluid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the instability of time-periodic motions is a general phenomenon, and it is not restricted to the flows considered here.
the instability is a result of the nonlinear coupling between the basic flow and the time-periodic perturbation.
the instability of a time-periodic flow is governed by the same type of equations which govern the instability to steady flow in a spatially varying flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability properties of a time-periodic flow are not simply a consequence of the stability properties of the steady state flow to which the periodic flow is a perturbation.
a time-periodic flow can induce a steady flow which is not present for the corresponding steady flow.
the instability of time-periodic flow is not a universal phenomenon, but is dependent upon the geometry of the flow.
